newsitem.title: UK: World LPG prices soften, buyers hold out for sprin.
newsitem.headline: World LPG prices soften, buyers hold out for sprin.

text.p: International Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices eased off early-year highs this week, with buyers holding back from the market in the hope of surviving until spring on close-to-empty tanks.

The Saudi contract price (CP), the key price marker for Gulf and Far East LPG sales, and an important market indicator for prices worldwide, was lowered for February, having touched record highs in January.
The BP Agreed Price (BPAP), the main European benchmark, was also reduced in February to $362 for propane and $244 for butane, BP said on Friday.
Saudi state oil company Saudi Aramco lowered the propane contract price for February by $10 to $320 a tonne, and its butane price by $25 to $305.
Nevertheless, the February CP for both products are over $100 a tonne higher than last year's levels.
Buyers in the Far East continued to keep purchases to the bare minimum, in anticipation of much lower prices in March, traders said.
"For seasonal reasons, if they can survive until early March on minimum stock levels, they can enjoy lower prices," said one trader active in the Far East market.
Dealers noted unusual co-operation between Japanese and South Korean buyers, including cargo swaps for optimising purchases in order to avoid extra purchases.
"They are getting smarter in their tactics," a trader said.
The Middle East Gulf fob market was weaker, with material fetching only a marginal premium, or even a discount to the CP.
Propane differentials c+f Japan were assessed fairly steady at CP +$30 a tonne, but trade was thin.
Chinese buying was also lacklustre with the approach of Chinese New Year already dampening interest, dealers said.

In Northwest Europe, values for small sea-going propane coasters dipped under the $400 a tonne level with sellers seen offering parcels at $390 fob U.K. on Friday. A deal at $422 a tonne on a cif basis earlier in the week translated to around $390 fob with freight estimated at between $30 and $35.
"There's lots of evidence of softer propane," said one trader. "I think it's going to go into freefall."
Two large propane cargoes were heard sold into the ARA market at in the mid $370s, some $25 down on last week.
"It's a combination of a few things, softer U.S. prices, a weaker Feb CP and poor Far East demand. And it's all been topped off by milder weather," said one European LPG trader.
The propane swaps market showed a steep backwardation still in place, with Feb swaps at $330-$340 a tonne cif NWE, and March swaps some $80 lower.
U.S. propane prices also continued to slide with spot Mont Belvieu prices languishing around 40 cents a gallon by the end of the week.
But thinly-talked butane bucked the trend in Europe this week, as prices firmed with volumes seen moving out of the region. Fob avails were pegged nearly $20 firmer at around $260 a tonne.
"The Brazilians came in and mopped up quite large volumes, which left the Europeans a little short for their own contracts, which pushed (the quotes) up," a dealer said.
French, Spanish and Portuguese buyers also picked up small parcels, traders said.
--Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5387
